author: EmuCore - Hub
title: TUTORIAL: Changing A Game's Visuals! (PCSX2 & MORE Texture Replacement)
summary: Razgriz Straitz demonstrates the creative side of PCSX2 texture replacement, moving beyond pack installation to editing a game’s visual assets with GIMP and returning the altered images through the emulator’s replacement path.

blocks.text: The eight-minute tutorial asks how a creator changes what a game displays rather than how a user copies an existing pack. GIMP is the named editing tool, making the workflow accessible without proprietary software. A useful conceptual loop emerges: capture or dump a texture, identify it among many similarly named files, edit while preserving dimensions and transparency, then reload it through PCSX2 to verify the result in context. That round trip is the foundation for restoration, translation mockups and original personal customization.

The description is extremely brief and does not identify the game, serial, PCSX2 build, dump settings, alpha format, mip levels or licensing of the demonstrated artwork. Changing extracted assets does not transfer redistribution rights, and an editor can easily break channels or seams that are invisible in a flat preview. Work from personal lawful data, retain untouched dumps, save editable sources separately and compare more than one scene. Current PCSX2 documentation should decide folder naming and supported formats, because interface details may outlive this recording poorly.
